```{r, tb_trend, include=FALSE}
df4 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(year_month = floor_date(date_of_registration, "month"))

tb_trend <- df4 %>%
  group_by(year_month) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = n(),
            deaths = sum(treatment_outcome == "Died", na.rm = TRUE))

print(tb_trend)
  
  
```


```{r, trend analysis, include=TRUE}

ggplot(tb_trend, aes(x = year_month)) +
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
df5 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(period = case_when(
    year < 2020 ~ "Pre-COVID",
    year >= 2020 & year <= 2022 ~ "COVID",
    TRUE ~ "Post-COVID"
  ))

# Summary table
summary_period <- df5 %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(total_cases = n(),
            deaths = sum(treatment_outcome == "Died", na.rm = TRUE),
            mortality_rate = deaths / total_cases * 100,
            .groups = "drop")

```

```{r, Summary of Cases and Mortality by Period, include=TRUE}
summary_period %>%

  ) %>%

    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center"
  )
```



```{r, categorical variables, include=FALSE}
categorical_vars1 <- df5 %>%
  select(where(~ is.character(.) | is.factor(.))) %>%
  names()

cat_summary <- function(data, var) {
  data %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(var))) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100, 2)) %>%
    arrange(desc(n))
}

```


```{r, function, include=FALSE}

# Function to visualise categorical summaries
plot_cat <- function(data, var) {
  data %>%
    group_by({{ var }}) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(as.character({{ var }}), -n), y = n, fill = as.character({{ var }}))) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)")), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Distribution of", deparse(substitute(var))),
      x = deparse(substitute(var)),
      y = "Count"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)
}
```

```{r,time variables, include=FALSE}
# Define COVID start date
covid_start <- as.Date("2020-03-01")

# Create key time variables
df6 <- df5 %>%
  mutate(
    date_of_registration = as_date(date_of_registration),  # convert to date
    reg_year = year(date_of_registration),
    reg_month = month(date_of_registration),
    reg_yearmonth = floor_date(date_of_registration, "month"),
    period = case_when(
      !is.na(date_of_registration) & date_of_registration >= covid_start ~ "COVID",
      !is.na(date_of_registration) & date_of_registration <  covid_start ~ "Pre-COVID",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```




```{r, include=FALSE}

# Count unique new registered cases per month and period
incidence_monthly <- df6 %>%
  filter(!is.na(date_of_registration)) %>%
  group_by(reg_yearmonth) %>%
  summarise(
    cases = n_distinct(serial_number),  # replace with your actual unique ID column
    period = ifelse(first(reg_yearmonth) >= floor_date(covid_start, "month"), "COVID", "Pre-COVID")
  ) %>%
  arrange(reg_yearmonth)



```


```{r,Monthly TB Registrations in Kenya, include=FALSE}
# Ensure reg_yearmonth is Date and add period classification
incidence_monthly <- incidence_monthly %>%
  mutate(
    reg_yearmonth = as.Date(reg_yearmonth),
    period = ifelse(reg_yearmonth >= floor_date(covid_start, "month"), "COVID", "Pre-COVID")
  )

# Plot incidence
p_incidence <- ggplot(incidence_monthly, aes(x = reg_yearmonth, y = cases, color = period, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = floor_date(covid_start, "month"), 
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linetype = "solid", size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b-%Y", date_breaks = "3 months", 
               expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.05))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly TB Registrations in Kenya",
    subtitle = paste("Dashed red line = COVID start:", covid_start),
    x = "Month",
    y = "Unique TB cases",
    color = "Period"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )


```


```{r,include=TRUE}
print(p_incidence)
```


```{r, Statistical test, include=FALSE}
# Statistical test: compare monthly counts pre vs during (t-test on monthly totals)
monthly_counts <- df6 %>%
  filter(!is.na(reg_yearmonth)) %>%
  group_by(reg_yearmonth) %>%
  summarise(cases = n_distinct(serial_number)) %>%
  mutate(period = ifelse(reg_yearmonth >= floor_date(covid_start, "month"),
                         "COVID", "Pre-COVID"))


tt_incidence <- t.test(cases ~ period, data = monthly_counts)
```

```{r, t-test, include=TRUE}

# Convert the t-test output into a data frame
tt_df <- data.frame(
  Statistic = tt_incidence$statistic,
  Parameter = tt_incidence$parameter,
  P_Value = tt_incidence$p.value,
  Conf_Lower = tt_incidence$conf.int[1],
  Conf_Upper = tt_incidence$conf.int[2],
  Mean_Group1 = tt_incidence$estimate[1],
  Mean_Group2 = tt_incidence$estimate[2]
)

# Create a nice kable table
kable(tt_df, 
      caption = "Tuberculosis Incidence T-Test Summary",
      align = "c",
      digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE,
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"))


```


```{r, include=FALSE}
# Identify deaths (common label variations)
df7 <- df6 %>%
  mutate(
    treatment_outcome_clean = tolower(as.character(treatment_outcome)),
    died_flag = case_when(
      grepl("died|death|dead", treatment_outcome_clean, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ 1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    )
  )

# Use treatment_outcome_date if available, otherwise use date_of_registration to assign period
df7 <- df7 %>%
  mutate(
    outcome_date = coalesce(treatment_outcome_date, date_of_registration),
    outcome_period = case_when(
      !is.na(outcome_date) & outcome_date >= covid_start ~ "COVID",
      !is.na(outcome_date) & outcome_date <  covid_start ~ "Pre-COVID",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

mortality_by_period <- df7 %>%
  filter(!is.na(outcome_period)) %>%
  group_by(outcome_period) %>%
  summarise(
    deaths = sum(died_flag, na.rm = TRUE),
    cases = n_distinct(serial_number),
    case_fatality_rate = deaths / cases
  )



```
